newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares edge up on small-cap buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares edge up on small-cap buying.

text.p: Jakarta share prices were marginally higher at the close on Tuesday on speculative buying of some small-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The composite index ended up 0.19 points, or 0.03 percent, at 623.81 points after dipping to 623.13 points earlier. Gainers led losers by 48 to 45, with 63 counters unchanged.
"Speculative buying of some second-liners helped the index close in positive territory. Otherwise the overall market was rather dull," one broker with a foreign brokerage firm said.
He said some foreign selling was noted in big-caps, but most foreign players preferred to stay sidelined.
Second-liners Multipolar, Branta Mulia and Tempo Scan were among the speculative focus of local players, brokers said.
Multipolar ended 275 rupiah higher at 1,500 rupiah on market talk of a possible stock split, one dealer said.
Another dealer, however, said the rise was possibly due to something else, as stock-split talk alone was unlikely to push the stock up sharply. Multipolar was not immediately available for comment.
Tempo Scan closed 200 rupiah higher at 3,750 on reports of a distribution agreement with Unilever, brokers said.

Branta Mulia continued its uptrend, gaining another 450 rupiah to close at 2,775 rupiah on confirmation that Du Pont of the United States had expressed interest in linking-up with the tyre cord firm, a local broker said.
Big-capitalised Sampoerna and Bimantara were among the losers following both local and foreign selling, broker said.
Indosat was unchanged at 6,350 rupiah as it held an analysts' meeting later on Tuesday to discuss its accounting rate.
